questions.question: scaling-strategy
questions.quote:
Schwarz rigidity uses the unit disk, but the assumption has radius
(r).  Rescale:

\[
g(w)=r^{-1}p(rw).
\]

questions.question: rotation-specializes-to-identity
questions.quote:
Here (\operatorname{dslope}(g,0,0)=g'(0)=1) and (g(0)=0), so the affine
slope is exactly (1) and the formula reduces to (g(w)=w); no arbitrary
textbook rotation remains.

questions.question: coefficient-extensionality
questions.quote:
Applying the degree-(N) coefficient
function to that equality makes their degree-(N) coefficients equal; these are
(c_N) and (0), since (N\ge2).  Thus (c_N=0), contrary to hypothesis.
